subject: Intermittent p99 surges + 429 surgechain impacting Pulse Health production
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@pulsehealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Pulse Health Ops <ops@pulsehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Production: p99 spike + 429s since 08:45 PDT (request ids attached)

Avery / Monica —

We're seeing a serious degradation in our integration with Redwood's Hosted API starting ~08:45 PDT this morning. p95 is elevated but p99 has jumped from ~230ms to ~1.8s for a subset of requests and we're getting bursts of 429s followed by timeouts. The pattern looks suspiciously like clients retrying which makes the tail worse — our telemetry shows repeated request_ids from a small pool of callers.

Attached is a CSV with the raw request IDs and timestamps (redwood_request_logs_20270619.csv) and a screenshot of our APM spike (p99_spike_screenshot_0620.png). Example request IDs: rwd-20270619-7f3a, rwd-20270619-7f3b.

This is hitting our production workflows (billing reconciliation and clinical notifications). We need immediate assistance. Can you open an incident with engineering and advise short-term mitigations (rate limit tuning, burst capacity, ephemeral fallback model)? We also need a timeline for a root cause investigation and an expected impact window — this is on our on-call rotation.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Platform Engineering
Pulse Health

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:24:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: p99 spike + 429s since 08:45 PDT (request ids attached)

Elena —

I'm really sorry you're seeing this. Thank you for the logs and the screenshot — that helps. I’ve opened an expedited incident (INF-4582) and looped in our SRE lead for immediate triage. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the 429s are coming back with "Retry-After" headers or if they're plain 429s? That changes the retry behavior we recommend.

Short-term we can:
- Temporarily raise your rate limit by 25% from our side (if you want us to do this now, confirm)
- Enable a per-customer token backoff rule so retries are de-duped for a short window
- Route a small percentage of your traffic to a lower-capacity but more latency-stable model variant as a fallback

I'll notify you of the SRE findings within 30 minutes. Monica — can you pull customer-level quota logs and confirm whether there were any sudden spikes in concurrent connections from Pulse Health's API key? Laura — FYI in case we need executive signal/credits.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:33:02 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: p99 spike + 429s since 08:45 PDT (request ids attached)

Avery / Team —

I've pulled the quota and connection logs. Summary so far:
- There was a ~3x request rate increase for Pulse Health between 08:42–08:51 PDT. Most calls are short-lived, but we see a cluster of repeated retries from ~08:44–08:50.
- 429 responses are plain 429s (no Retry-After header), which means client libraries are likely doing exponential backoff but still generating repeated traffic that amplifies tail latency.
- We can temporarily raise the quota for PH key key_ph_2891 by 30% under a short-lived policy; it will take ~2 minutes to propagate.

I've attached a small export (pulse_health_map.txt) with per-minute counts and sample request ids. Rishi — requesting SLO/tiering look and whether we should flip a fallback routing policy now.

Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 10:02:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: p99 spike + 429s since 08:45 PDT (request ids attached)

Team —

Quick root-cause notes from initial triage (INF-4582):
- Observed behavior is classic retry amplification against our rate-limiter frontier. When a subset of requests hit the rate limiter and return 429s without Retry-After semantics, upstream clients retry aggressively. That increases queueing and spikes tail latency (p99) even for non-retried traffic.
- The impacted model shard experienced temporary saturation on a small set of GPU workers between 08:43–08:49 PDT. There were also a handful of long-running KV-cache misses which drove CPU spikes during fetches.

Immediate mitigations we applied (10:00 PDT):
- Flipped per-customer soft limits to allow +30% throughput for key_ph_2891 (Monica did the policy change)
- Enabled short-lived slow-path de-dup window (100ms) to collapse near-duplicate retries at the frontend LB
- Deployed a targeted routing rule to route 10% of Pulse Health traffic to the quantized model variant (slightly lower quality, better latency tail)

Next steps / asks:
- We need Pulse Health to apply a client-side retry guard (prefer a capped jitter backoff and honor 429/Retry-After when present). If you can't change clients quickly, we can extend the de-dup window server-side for 1 hour.
- Engineering will follow up with a detailed RCA and a plan to improve Retry-After header coverage + make rate-limit responses more informative.

I'll prepare an ops timeline and a preliminary RCA memo by EOD PT. Laura — please advise on whether a service credit / one-off SLA concession and an exec sync are required now.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: p99 spike + 429s since 08:45 PDT (request ids attached)

Elena —

Quick update and actions we've taken across the window:
- We saw the initial surge on Friday morning and applied short-term mitigations (quota bump, de-dup window, fallback routing). These reduced visible 429s and brought your p99 down from 1.8s to ~320ms on the fallback mix.
- Rishi's team is drafting an RCA (linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4582). We'll share the detailed timeline and permanent mitigations by EOD Monday.
- For an immediate safety net, we recommend Pulse Health enable a client-side capped-jitter backoff and implement a 2s global retry cap during recovery windows. If you want, we can push a server-side extended de-dup window for 60 minutes when you detect a spike — say the word and we’ll enable it.
- Laura is onboarding for executive coordination; if a credit or SLA concession is required we'll make a formal request.

Thanks for your patience and the detailed logs — they made triage faster. Please ping me if you want a 1:1 incident debrief.

Best,
Avery Johnson
